correctness.rationale: The fixed 12-edge cube has exactly eight forbidden incident stars. Exhaustive checking of all nonempty 12-bit masks yields 1,698 faces, with 847 disjoint cover-relation matching pairs and four critical faces of dimensions 0,5,5,5. The complete oriented face-poset Hasse graph has 7,980 covers and a verified 1,698-element directed topological ordering, certifying acyclicity. Finite discrete Morse theory therefore gives a CW model with only one vertex and three five-cells, necessarily trivially attached, which is exactly a wedge of three five-spheres. Independent mod-two boundary ranks [11,55,157,266,250,99,9] confirm the corresponding field Betti vector, but the homotopy proof does not depend on that check. All proofs and certificates are within verify.py, certificate.json, verification_output.txt.

value.rationale: The eight-vertex cube is a canonical cubic test case for the first nontrivial relaxation of matching complexes. The same object is the cuboctahedral 3-clique-free complex, beyond the recent chordal shellability theory. Despite 7-dimensional maximal faces and a nonpure facet structure, its integral homotopy type has only three 5-sphere summands, a meaningful topological invariant not determined by its f-vector or routine inclusion in a complete-bipartite matching complex. The complete small natural classification and a reusable exhaustive proof certificate are valuable without claiming an infinite family.
